question: On 12 June 2026, Anthropic restricted EU users’ access to its most advanced AI models, Mythos and Fables, following a US government directive limiting exports of these technologies in the interest of national security.

The Commission stated that it has taken note of this action and that it reinforces calls for greater technological sovereignty through instruments such as the Artificial Intelligence Act, the Cyber Resilience Act and the NIS 2 Directive. While Europe is working to reduce external dependencies on foreign providers, questions remain regarding Anthropic’s current restrictions. 1.
Is the Commission working to ensure that EU users’ data, prompts and other account information are not retained by Anthropic?

During this transition period towards greater technological sovereignty, what contingency plans does the Commission have to protect the data of EU citizens and businesses from being controlled by unilateral decisions taken by foreign governments?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.10.2026) As advances in frontier AI models offer opportunities as well as novel and heightened risks for cybersecurity, the Commission adopted on 7 July 2026 an Action Plan on Cybersecurity and AI1. A key priority of the Commission is to ensure that frontier AI models are safe, accessible and deployable for cybersecurity in Europe.

The Action Plan proposes a Blueprint as a framework for structured access to advanced AI capabilities for cybersecurity purposes which will include criteria that should be considered for granting access to European players.

As part of the Blueprint, the Commission intends to propose processes and restrictions on the handling of information such as prompts, uploaded files and outputs, thus also ensuring the privacy and safety of potentially critical European information. The ability to develop and deploy AI-powered cybersecurity solutions is becoming a strategic enabler of cyber resilience and sovereignty.

As part of the Tech Sovereignty Package of 3 June 2026, the Commission proposed the Cloud and AI Development Act2 which would expand EU data centre capacity and cloud and AI autonomy, supporting the wider deployment of AI – including cyber-related tools and applications. The Action Plan aims to scale European AI capabilities for cybersecurity.

This includes boosting the European ecosystem around AI-powered cybersecurity solutions, e.g. through the grand challenge on AI-assisted vulnerability remediation, building European frontier capabilities and boosting cybersecurity skills for the age of AI.

In the meantime, European players should already start using available AI capabilities, including through open-source models, to detect vulnerabilities and to improve the detection and prevention of cyberattacks.
